item.title: Ocasio-Cortez Donates to N.Y. Democrats, Will Barnstorm State Ahead of Midterms
item.description: The news has reignited speculation about whether the progressive representative from the Bronx is considering a run for senator or president.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Tailyr Irvine for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York has become the subject of great speculation over whether she will run for president or senator in 2028.

item.title: Abortion Rights Activists in Idaho Find Their Pitch: Bring Back the Doctors
item.description: Organizers of a referendum to repeal an abortion ban in deep-red Idaho are far more focused on how the ban has broadly affected health care in the state.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Idaho Legislature enacted one of the strictest abortion bans in the country, criminalizing abortion for doctors. Since then, the number of ob-gyns has plunged.

item.title: Ashley Hinson, a Republican ‘Minivan-Driving Mom,’ Steers Away From Trump in Midterm Elections
item.description: Representative Ashley Hinson is hoping to keep a crucial Senate seat red in Iowa, where the president has created major headwinds for her party.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: KC McGinnis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Ashley Hinson of Iowa is locked in a tight race against Josh Turek, a Democratic state representative, that could be crucial for Senate control.

item.title: How Karaoke Became a Healing Balm for the Exonerated Community
item.description: A night of belting out R&B and pop hits has become a re-entry ritual and celebration of life for some wrongly imprisoned men and women thrust back into society.
item.dc:creator: Maya King
item.media:credit: Madison Swart for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jorge Linares, left, singing karaoke with Jeffrey Deskovic, right, during a celebration with the Innocence Project marking the 20th anniversary of Mr. Deskovic’s exoneration.

item.title: Trump Moves Ahead With F-35 Jet Sales to Saudi Arabia Despite Intelligence Concerns
item.description: U.S. intelligence agencies have warned in internal reports that China could acquire or steal U.S. warplane technology if F-35 jets are sent to Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong
item.media:description: If the production and delivery of the planes is completed, which would take years, Saudi Arabia would be only the second country in the Middle East to have F-35 jets, after Israel.

item.title: Immigration Officer Found Guilty of Sexually Assaulting and Robbing Women
item.description: The officer, a Customs and Border Protection agent at a Chicago airport, was accused of assaulting and threatening four women, all of Chinese descent, at hotel rooms in 2022.
item.dc:creator: Madaleine Rubin
item.media:description: Luis Uribe was working at O’Hare International Airport in Chicago as a Customs and Border Protection officer at the time of the crimes.

item.title: Former Institute of Peace Workers Warn Trump May Push to Engrave Name on Building
item.description: As part of a lawsuit, the workers have asked a federal court to stop any plans to engrave the building with President Trump’s name.
item.dc:creator: Aishvarya Kavi
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: President Trump’s name was adhered to the Institute of Peace building in December in large, silver letters alongside engraved letters identifying the institute.

item.title: S.U.V. Driver Charged With Murder in Los Angeles Bus Crash
item.description: Prosecutors said the driver was impaired by drugs and ran a red light before ramming a city bus on Tuesday. Two people died. Compounding the tragedy, a news helicopter also crashed.
item.dc:creator: Livia Albeck-Ripka
item.category: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
item.media:credit: Ronaldo Bolanos/Los Angeles Times, via Getty Images
item.media:description: An S.U.V. slammed into a bus in Chatsworth, a neighborhood in the San Fernando Valley region of Los Angeles, on Tuesday evening.

item.title: Jury Reaches Mixed Verdict in Death of Reporter Covering Super Bowl
item.description: The Telemundo reporter, Adan Manzano, was found in his hotel room just before the 2025 Super Bowl in New Orleans.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.media:credit: Telemundo Kansas City, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Adan Manzano, a reporter for Telemundo Kansas City, was found dead on Feb. 5, 2025, in his hotel room.

item.title: Alabama Executes Inmate After Supreme Court Blocked Last Attempt
item.description: Jeffery Lee had raised concerns about use of nitrogen gas and the legacy of an abandoned practice that allowed judges to override juries on death sentences.
item.dc:creator: Rick Rojas
item.media:description: The Death Penalty Action group in June, protesting the execution of Jeffrey Lee in Alabama.

item.title: Virginia Attorney General: D.H.S. Likely Broke State Law in Voter Fraud Investigation
item.description: The department has pulled hundreds of agents from their regular duties to find noncitizens on the voter rolls, despite decades of evidence that widespread voter fraud is exceptionally rare in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:description: Attorney General Jay Jones of Virginia said a federal hunt for noncitizens on state voter rolls “potentially violates several Virginia laws.”

item.title: Blanche’s Political Campaigning Breaks an Ethical Norm Going Back to Watergate
item.description: The attorney general’s campaign politicking for Republicans adds to the degradation of post-Watergate values at the Justice Department.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Savage
item.media:description: Attorney General Todd Blanche speaking last week on the first day of the Republican midterm convention.

item.title: Trump Wants Putin to End the War. He May Offer Russia Business Deals First.
item.description: A new sanctions bill is meant to pressure President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia to end the war in Ukraine. But President Trump is doubling down on a different approach: offering enticements to Russia.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski
item.media:description: President Donald Trump shaking hands with President Vladimir Putin of Russia during their meeting in Alaska last year.

item.title: Montana Ballot Measure Would Strike at Political ‘Dark Money’
item.description: A measure aimed at stemming the tide of corporate money in politics will be on the November ballot. Opponents say it violates a high court ruling.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.category: Citizens United v Federal Election Commission (Supreme Court Decision)
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: Montana voters will be asked whether to bar businesses, unions and nonprofit groups from donating to political candidates or parties.

item.title: Man Who Attacked Ilhan Omar Sentenced to 14 Months After Plea Deal
item.description: Anthony J. Kazmierczak sprayed vinegar at Ms. Omar while she was speaking at a Minneapolis town hall in January. He pleaded guilty to assault in May.
item.dc:creator: Sejal Govindarao
item.media:credit: Victor J. Blue for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthony J. Kazmierczak was detained after squirting vinegar on Representative Ilhan Omar during a town hall in Minneapolis in January.

item.title: Yosemite Wildfire Grows to Nearly 1,200 Acres
item.description: The blaze has forced trail closures and reduced air quality in sections of the California national park.
item.dc:creator: Soumya Karlamangla and Amy Graff
item.media:description: A view of the Merced River in Yosemite National Park in June.

item.title: Hasan Piker’s Comments Create Headaches for Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Under pressure, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan this week rejected Hasan Piker’s argument that the U.S. has caused more terror than Al Qaeda.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Emily Elconin for The New York Times
item.media:description: Some Democrats have pressured Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to fully disavow Hasan Piker after his comments on terrorism.

item.title: ICE Agent Charged in Shooting Appears In Court in Minnesota
item.description: Christian Castro, the agent charged in the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant in January, faces felony charges in state and federal courts. He was released from jail a day after his arrest.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: The cases against Christian Castro, an immigration agent, stem from a shooting in January that injured Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, who is standing on the right in the photo.

item.title: The Public Charge Rule: How Trump’s Green Card Policy Could Affect Immigrant Families
item.description: The policy, set to take effect Friday, would give immigration officers broader authority to deny permanent residency to people using public benefits.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: A parcel at a Boston-area food bank seen in April. The policy is the Trump administration’s latest effort to restrict legal immigration and deter people from signing up for welfare programs such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program.

item.title: At Gettysburg, a Reporter Captured a Nation’s Loss, and His Own
item.description: Samuel Wilkeson Jr. filed a report for The Times from the battlefield. Then he went looking for a Union officer, his son.
item.dc:creator: Dan Barry

item.title: Trump Air Force One Photos Fuel Kennedy Center Demolition Speculation
item.description: Images captured through the windows of Air Force One showed President Trump reviewing a poster with the title “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED.”
item.dc:creator: Shawn McCreesh
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: President Trump aboard Air Force One after landing at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on Wednesday night.

item.title: White House Pulls Nomination of Lance Schroyer, Ally of Markwayne Mullin, for ICE Director
item.description: President Trump nominated Lance Schroyer, a former law enforcement officer from Oklahoma, less than three months ago.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:description: Lance Schroyer in 2016. Mr. Schroyer had not previously worked at ICE.

item.title: Jon Kyl, Senator Known for His Skills Behind the Scenes, Dies at 84
item.description: The Arizona politician rose to the second-highest position in the Republican-held Senate caucus thanks to his policy smarts and deft political sensibilities.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:description: Jon Kyl, often described as a low-key workhorse, in 2018. “You can accomplish a lot if you’re not necessarily out in front on everything,” he once said.

item.title: Are Trump’s Official Papers His Personal Property?
item.description: The administration argues that presidential papers are like those of Supreme Court justices.
item.dc:creator: Adam Liptak

item.title: G.O.P. Representative Breaks With Trump in Ad Criticizing the Immigration Crackdown
item.description: Representative María Elvira Salazar, a three-term representative from Miami, won re-election by 20 percentage points in 2024. Her ad suggests worry among some Republicans about their standing with Hispanic voters.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei, Michael Gold and Shane Goldmacher
item.media:description: Representative María Elvira Salazar, a Florida Republican, released a television ad on Thursday assailing President Trump’s immigration crackdown.

item.title: Afghan Sentenced to 20 Years After Mixed Verdict in 2021 Kabul Attack Case
item.description: A jury had split on whether Mohammad Sharifullah was to blame in a deadly bombing but found him guilty of aiding the terrorist group ISIS-K.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe
item.media:description: Portraits of some of the U.S. service members who were killed in a 2021 suicide bombing at an airport in Kabul, Afghanistan, are seen at a posthumous award ceremony at the Capitol in 2024.

item.title: For a Border Tribe, Trump’s Wall Is a Betrayal: ‘They Want to Erase Us’
item.description: An escalating confrontation on Native land southwest of Tucson threatens to upend decades of uneasy cooperation between the Tohono O’odham Nation and the United States.
item.dc:creator: Reis Thebault and Anna Watts
item.media:description: “It’s like me bulldozing right through the Arlington Cemetery,” said Verlon Jose, the chairman of the Tohono O’odham Nation.
